title: A quasi-separated space with an etale field atlas is a field spectrum
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $Y$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $L$ be a field [def-weil-field] with an $S$-morphism $q:\operatorname{Spec}L\to Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume $q$ is representable, surjective and etale in the scheme-test sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume $Y$ is quasi-separated: its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact, meaning that its pullback along every affine test scheme has quasi-compact underlying topological space [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Then there is a subfield $k\subseteq L$ and an isomorphism $Y\cong\operatorname{Spec}k$ over $S$ under which $q$ is induced by the inclusion $k\hookrightarrow L$. The extension $L/k$ is finite separable: it has finite vector-space dimension and the minimal polynomial of each element has no repeated root in an algebraic closure. No finite-type hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03DZ (lemma-point-like-spaces), statement and its displayed invariant subfield in the proof.

proof.text: Put $U=\operatorname{Spec}L$ and $R=U\times_Y U$. Apply [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation] to the given representable surjective etale $S$-map $q$. It gives a representing scheme $R$, surjective etale projections $s,t:R\to U$, and a sectionwise equivalence relation $(s,t):R\to U\times_S U$. It also identifies $Y$, with its specified map from $U$, with the fppf sheaf quotient $U/R$. All these statements are over the original scheme $S$.

The statement of [def-sfb-space-absolute-quasi-separated] identifies quasi-compactness of the absolute diagonal with the affine-test criterion, for algebraic spaces over an arbitrary scheme $S$. Apply that criterion to the two copies of the affine $S$-scheme $U$ and the maps $q,q$. Their sheaf fibre product is precisely the represented scheme $R$ from step 1, so $R$ is quasi-compact. This uses absolute quasi-separatedness, exactly the hypothesis of the item, and imposes no separation or finite-type assumption on $S$.

source.place: Tag 0AHR (lemma-characterize-quasi-separated), equivalence (1) and (3); quasi-compactness step in Tag 03DZ (lemma-point-like-spaces).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] to $s:R\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ at the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Its residue field is $L$, and base change by its identity identifies this fibre with $R$. Thus $R$ is the disjoint union of its one-point open subschemes $\operatorname{Spec}L_i$, where each $L_i/L$ via $s$ is finite separable. The cover of $R$ by these singleton opens has a finite subcover by step 2; hence there are only finitely many points, indexed by a finite set $I$. Apply the same cited statement to $t$ at the unique point of $U$. It says that the same intrinsic residue fields $L_i$ are finite separable over $L$ also via $t$. The diagonal section $U\to R$ shows that $I$ is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), clause (2); finite-index argument in spaces-properties.tex Tag 03DZ (lemma-point-like-spaces).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], $R\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ for $B=\prod_{i\in I}L_i$. Under either structural map $L\to B$, a choice of a finite $L$-basis of each $L_i$ gives a finite basis of $B$ by placing those basis elements in their respective coordinates. Consequently $s$ and $t$ are finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]: both source and target are affine and the corresponding algebra is a finite module. They are flat and locally of finite presentation because they are etale, by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The definition [def-pc-finite-locally-free] therefore makes both projections finite locally free. This verifies all the geometric hypotheses needed for the affine-relation quotient theorem.

source.place: Tag 03DZ (lemma-point-like-spaces), finite locally free projections before application of Tag 03BM; finite coproduct identification: Schemes Tag 01I5 (lemma-disjoint-union-affines).

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-finite-flat-affine-relation-quotient] to the affine $S$-schemes $U=\operatorname{Spec}L$, $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and the relation of step 1, using step 4 for finite local freeness. It identifies the quotient with $\operatorname{Spec}C$, where $C=\{a\in L:s^\sharp(a)=t^\sharp(a)\}$, and identifies its quotient map with the map induced by $C\subseteq L$, all over $S$. The two quotient identifications give $Y\cong\operatorname{Spec}C$ with the required compatibility with $q$. The subring $C$ contains $0,1$ and is closed under addition and multiplication because $s^\sharp,t^\sharp$ are ring maps. For $0\ne a\in C$, these maps carry $a^{-1}$ to the inverses of their common value at $a$, so their values at $a^{-1}$ are equal. Hence $C$ is a subfield $k\subseteq L$.

source.place: Tag 03BM (proposition-finite-flat-equivalence), as used in spaces-properties.tex Tag 03DZ (lemma-point-like-spaces); the displayed invariant subfield and its closure under inverses.

proof.text: Under this isomorphism, the given etale map $q$ is $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ induced by inclusion. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] at the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, whose residue field is $k$. The fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}L$, with its single residue field $L$. The cited statement makes $L/k$ finite and every element a root of a separable polynomial over $k$. Its minimal polynomial divides such a polynomial and therefore has no repeated root. These are exactly the two required clauses of finite separability.

source.place: Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), clause (2), applied to the quotient map in Tag 03DZ (lemma-point-like-spaces).

proof_origin.place: Tag 03DZ (lemma-point-like-spaces), full proof, with absolute quasi-separatedness applied via Tag 0AHR and finite separability spelled out via Tag 02GL.

lean.statement: theorem pointlike_quasiseparated_space_field {S : Scheme.{u}} (Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (L : Type u) [Field L] (a : Spec (CommRingCat.of L) ⟶ S) (q : yoneda.obj (Over.mk a) ⟶ Y.obj.obj) (hq : IsEtale q) (hsur : IsSurjective q) (hY : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated Y) : ∃ (k : Subfield L) (b : Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ S) (h : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom k.subtype) ≫ b = a) (e : Y.obj.obj ≅ yoneda.obj (Over.mk b)), q ≫ e.hom = yoneda.map (Over.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom k.subtype)) h) ∧ FiniteDimensional k L ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable k L
